title: lekka recipe
description: A recipe as a flow: ingredients go into a step, its result goes into the next step, and the last step finishes the dish. GUIDE.md says how to write one.

title.description: The name of the dish, without what it yields.

yields.description: What it makes, a number and what of: "12 pancakes", "1 loaf", "4 servings".

source.description: Where the recipe came from, usually its web address.

aliases.description: Other names somebody might search for it under.

notes.description: What is worth knowing about the recipe as a whole and is not part of the flow.

preparations.description: What to know or do before the first step, in the order it is done: when to start ("start the evening before"), a tin to ready, an oven to heat for a bake that begins at once. The only place for a preparation: what happens later is said in the sentence of the step it happens during.

root.description: The last step. Everything else flows into it.

aside.description: What you must know but do not do. On a step: how, or until when ("covered", "until doubled"), shown beside it in the table; say it in its sentence too. On an ingredient: what matters before cooking, to choose, buy or prepare it ("Type 550", "chopped"); it is shown with the ingredient list, never in the steps.

step.description: Something done to what flows into it. At least one ingredient must flow into it, directly or through earlier steps.
The short form, the verb first, then its parameters: "bake 200 °C 40 min". It labels the step in the table, and its time becomes a timer.

sentence.description: The step as a cook would write it, in the recipe's language: every ingredient this step takes named once in braces, exactly as its name is written: "mix {flour}, {salt} and {dry yeast}". No amounts: each ingredient is listed under the sentence with its own. What earlier steps made is named in plain words, "the dough"; what to do meanwhile is said too, "meanwhile heat the oven to 220 °C". Lower case, no full stop.

children.description: What flows into this step, in the order it joins: ingredients and earlier steps.

ingredient.description: One use of something that goes into the food. Used twice, it is two ingredients.

What you reach for when the step comes, and all the step shows besides the amount: a noun and any word that changes which thing you take ("black pepper", "lukewarm water"). What matters only before cooking goes in the aside.

amount.description: A number and a unit ("250 g"), a range ("40-60 g"), a count ("2"), or words ("to taste"). Decimals, not fractions: "0.5 l". Leave it out when there is none.

preparation.description: Something to know or do before the first step, that nothing flows from: "start the evening before", "grease a loaf tin".
